content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E027 (Jacob Mann) requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
Note 1: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
Note 2: employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read.

These conflict. The Security DB note says contractor with basic training, differing from earlier note. The policy: contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → max read. Full-time Engineer → up to write, admin if role owns system. Engineer owns Source Code, so admin allowed, but requested write.

The conflicting notes: which to trust? The Approver needs to decide. Note 2 says Security DB shows contractor with basic security training, noting it differs from the earlier note claiming full-time. Security DB is likely authoritative for employment type. Given the security note, E027 is a contractor with basic training, so max access is read. Requested write is above max, so grant max = read.

So decision: read.

Reason: The security note indicates contractor with basic training; contractors without advanced training max is read. Since write was requested but exceeds the max, grant read.
